title: Ancient Trees in Turkey: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Istanbul's oldest living thing is a plane put at 1,300 years, older than the city's Ottoman name by seven centuries. 14 trees mapped.
intro: Istanbul's oldest living thing is an oriental plane put at 1,300 to 1,400 years, which predates the city's Ottoman name by seven centuries. It stands inside a university forestry station at Bahcekoy, and a stranger one grows nearby: the Ahtapot Cinar, whose lowest branches touched the ground centuries ago, thickened where they landed, and now read as seven trunks sharing a single root system. Turkey keeps a national Monument Tree register that carries ages, so the numbers here are firmer than in most of Europe. The famous exception is Topkapi's plane in the First Courtyard, the one said to have witnessed the conquest of 1453, which has been dead for about a century. Fourteen trees mapped, all in Istanbul, and eight of them are planes.
